taskDescription: Arrange the steps of dietary triacylglycerol digestion and absorption in their correct sequence.
paragraphs: Fat entering the duodenum triggers CCK release, which contracts the gallbladder and stimulates pancreatic secretion.
Bile salts coat and emulsify fat droplets, vastly increasing the surface area for enzymatic attack.
Pancreatic lipase, anchored by colipase, hydrolyses positions 1 and 3 to yield 2-monoacylglycerol and two free fatty acids.
Mixed micelles formed with bile salts carry the products across the unstirred water layer to the jejunal brush border.
Inside the enterocyte, long-chain fatty acids are re-esterified to triacylglycerol and packaged with ApoB-48 into chylomicrons.
Chylomicrons enter the intestinal lacteals and reach the blood via the thoracic duct.

overallFeedback.feedback: Dietary fat digestion follows a strict sequence: CCK triggers bile and enzyme delivery, bile salts emulsify the fat, lipase with colipase hydrolyses positions 1 and 3 (not all three bonds), micelles ferry the products to the brush border, the enterocyte re-packages them with ApoB-48 into chylomicrons, and these travel via lymph — not portal blood — explaining why fat-soluble vitamins also depend on this intact pathway.
